sections.content:
You know emotional reactions with the subjunctive from A2 Unit 27 (*me alegra que*, *me encanta que*, *me molesta que*) and exclamations with *¡Qué* + noun/adjective + *que* + subjunctive from B2 Unit 6 (*¡Qué alegría que...*, *¡Qué pena que...*). In sarcastic speech, speakers invert these warm formulas to express irritation or disbelief.

The grammar does not change when the tone turns sarcastic: **mock delight** still triggers the subjunctive (*¡Me encanta que hayan cambiado la hora sin avisar!* = "I just love how they changed the time without telling us!"; *¡Qué maravilla que tengamos otra reunión el viernes por la tarde!*). Even though the event actually happened, the emotional frame keeps the subjunctive (present for current/future, present perfect for completed past).

Alongside those clauses, everyday Spanish uses fixed sarcastic exclamations that stand alone: *¡Qué casualidad!* ("What a coincidence!"), *¡Qué gracia!* ("How funny!"—usually meaning not funny at all), *¡A buena hora!* ("A fine time to do that—far too late!"), and *¡Faltaría más!* (polite "Of course!" or ironic "That would be the last straw!").

sections.title: Mock reactions and fixed sarcastic exclamations
rows: *¡Me encanta que llegues siempre cuando ya terminamos!*
*¡Qué maravilla que hayan olvidado enviar el documento!*
*Justo se enfermó el día de la mudanza: ¡qué casualidad!*
*¿Ahora avisas que no vienes? ¡A buena hora!*

items.spanish: ¡Qué maravilla que hayan elegido la hora más difícil para todos!
items.english: How wonderful that they chose the hardest time for everyone!

items.spanish: Me encanta que nadie lea las instrucciones antes de preguntar.
items.english: I just love how nobody reads the instructions before asking.

items.spanish: ¿Nos avisan del cambio diez minutos antes del examen? ¡A buena hora!
items.english: They tell us about the change ten minutes before the exam? A fine time!

items.spanish: Dice que fue un error sin importancia: ¡qué gracia tiene ese disparate!
items.english: He says it was an unimportant mistake: how funny that absurdity is!

sections.content: Do not drop into the indicative when a *¡Qué maravilla que...!* or *¡Me encanta que...!* remark is sarcastic (*¡Qué maravilla que olvidaron el informe!* ✗ → *¡Qué maravilla que hayan olvidado el informe!* ✓). Sarcasm flips the meaning, never the subjunctive.
